clue.text: Six-footer cooks train outside rear of brasserie

parts.note: to devil food is to cook it with hot spices, as in devilled kidneys
to coach someone is to train them
hors is French for outside, as in hors d'oeuvre

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its tail end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of brasserie

explanation.surface: A very tall chef cooking on a train, near the back of the dining car.
explanation.walkthrough: The French brasserie nudges the solver towards French, which is where the word for outside comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: This large black beetle is an insect, and every insect walks on six legs, so it is jokingly a creature with six feet.

clue.text: Decided on a title for boosting issues

indicators.note: boosting lifts something up, and in a down entry lifting the letters reads them from bottom to top

parts.note: to set a date is to decide on it
taken as written
a title is a name

explanation.surface: Someone settling on a book title to give the publication a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase SET A NAME is turned upside down, not each word separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that emanates flows out or comes forth from a source, just as a verb meaning issues does.

clue.text: I see a lot of paperwork to secure the City cooler

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the outer letters grip the City between them

parts.note: taken as written
see is pronounced like the letter C
EC is the postcode area for the City of London, its financial district
a ream is a large quantity of paper, five hundred sheets

explanation.surface: An office worker eyeing a mountain of documents needed to land a City deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The City with a capital C is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen dessert eaten on a hot day chills you down, so it is something that cools.

clue.text: Where Descartes did his course in self- actualisation?

definitions.text: Where Descartes did his course in self- actualisation?

parts.note: surface reading: the college where the French philosopher studied
setter's reading: Descartes reasoned 'I think, therefore I am', so thinking was how he proved he existed

explanation.walkthrough: Self-actualisation sounds like a self-help course; for Descartes, existence followed from thinking, so his learning ground is a place of thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally means a body of shared opinion or a philosophical movement, which fits a philosopher.

clue.text: Foot transplant causing lamb to become lame?

parts.note: the transplant takes the final letter out of lamb
one letter acting as another, a swap spoken as 'this as that'
the letter that arrives in its place, turning lamb into lame

explanation.surface: A foot transplant goes badly wrong and leaves a young sheep limping.
explanation.walkthrough: Turning lamb into lame means putting B as E, and read as a word that instruction is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The base of a column or mountain is its lowest part, its foot.

clue.text: A forgotten Earth, was it once, land not as developed?

definitions.text: A forgotten Earth, was it once, land not as developed?

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so the letters are rebuilt in another order
something forgotten is left out, so the letter A is dropped from the word beside it
not means without, so the two letters a and s are taken away from the neighbouring word

parts.note: taken as written, before its A goes
taken as written, before its A and S go
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Musing on a lost, primitive Earth: a land less developed than it is today.
explanation.walkthrough: Earth loses its A and was loses AS, leaving just W; the rest is rearranged. The whole clue also describes the answer, an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth long ago, a half-forgotten land less developed than now, is a description of antiquity and its civilisations.

clue.text: Two details of origin when looking up Rioja here?

indicators.note: looking up in a down entry means the letters climb from bottom to top

parts.note: your age is one detail on an identity form
DOB, date of birth, is the other detail recording where your life began
surface padding that points the definition at a Spanish wine

explanation.surface: Checking the label of a Rioja for its vintage and where it came from.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is simply 'here', pointing at the place where you would find Rioja: a Spanish wine shop or cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine cellar or wine shop, the very place a bottle of Rioja would be found.

clue.text: Salvation Army raised importance for old people sitting

indicators.note: something raised is lifted upwards, and in a down entry that runs the letters bottom to top

parts.note: SA is the standard abbreviation for the Salvation Army
size can mean magnitude or significance

explanation.surface: The Salvation Army stepping up its care for elderly people who sit all day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old people' looks like pensioners, but 'old' marks a historical term and 'people sitting' is a court in session.
explanation.definitionFit: The assizes were periodic court sessions held across England and Wales until 1972, so a historical sitting of judges.

clue.text: See 1
Drunk hangs around Elephant's Head (he has one)

definitions.text: Drunk hangs around Elephant's Head (he has one)

indicators.note: around places the rearranged letters on either side of the kept letter
a drunk person staggers about, so the letters of the next word reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, before it is rearranged

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Elephant

explanation.surface: A drunk dangling around a pub called the Elephant's Head, with a parenthetical aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed aside turns the whole clue into a description: the Hindu god in question has an elephant's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindu deity of wisdom and new beginnings is always depicted with the head of an elephant on a human body.

clue.text: Jots on front of Otello programme? India rubber's needed before a stage production

indicators.note: a jot is a tiny amount, and taking only the front of each word leaves its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Otello
the first letter of programme
a rubber is a pencil eraser in British English
India is the NATO alphabet word for I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pencil notes scribbled on a Verdi programme, and someone calling for an India-rubber eraser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'India rubber' reads as one thing, but India and rubber give separate pieces; in Britain a rubber is an eraser.
explanation.definitionFit: This is serious Italian opera of the 18th century, a genre of staged musical drama, so a stage production.

clue.text: Old HMRC busts were endowed with zero style

indicators.note: to bust into somewhere is to break in, so one piece forces its way inside the other

parts.note: to be endowed with something is to have it
HMRC, the UK tax authority, used to be the Inland Revenue
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Tax inspectors raiding people who were given money with nothing to show for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstyle is a way of arranging the hair, and an informal word for a styled head of hair is this one.

clue.text: Where fold receives aura of deity into a small place of worship?

definitions.text: Where fold receives aura of deity into a small place of worship?

indicators.note: something that receives takes others in, so the fold opens to hold what follows

parts.note: a lapel is the folded-back part of a jacket front

indicators.note: an aura surrounds something, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of deity
CH is the abbreviation for church
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sheep fold taking in the glow of a god, turning into a tiny shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: Fold suggests sheep or a church flock, but here it is the fold on a jacket; the whole clue also describes where the answer is found.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel dedicated to the Virgin Mary inside a larger church or cathedral is a small place of worship within a bigger one.

clue.text: Woman in Vatican retiring, and staying on

indicators.note: staying means remaining inside, so the little word sits within the other
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman at the Vatican who will not retire and stays on in post.
explanation.definitionFit: Donna is the Italian word for a lady, the language spoken in Vatican City.

clue.text: Proceed to care for relation over 3

indicators.note: to care for something is to hold it close, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: to go is to proceed

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the relation is read backwards

parts.note: a relation is an account or story, a tale

explanation.surface: Being told to go and look after an older relative.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 3 points to the answer of 3 down, ICE CREAM. Relation looks like a family member but is a narrative.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelato is the Italian form of a frozen dessert, so it is one kind of the 3 down answer.

clue.text: Injury, but not from criminal

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the following word is cut out

parts.note: an offence is a wrong done to someone, an injury to their feelings
of can mean from, as in 'of noble birth'

explanation.surface: Someone injured, though not by any criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a fence is a criminal who receives and sells on stolen goods.

clue.text: In elevation use painter to bring brass hats together

indicators.note: elevation raises something, and in a down entry that runs the letters upwards

parts.note: a painter is the rope at a boat's bow, used to tie it up
to draw something is to pull or bring it

explanation.surface: An artist making a drawing that gathers top military brass for a portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: Painter looks like an artist but is a mooring rope. Brass hats are senior officers.
explanation.definitionFit: The wardroom is the mess on a warship where commissioned officers gather, so it is where senior ranks meet.

clue.text: Miscellany for us individually aces super crisp cask!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an assortment of assorted things

definitions.text: for us individually aces super crisp cask
definitions.note: a cryptic description: each of these four words is itself a jumbled container
definitions.meaning: second meaning: taken one at a time, aces, super, crisp and cask each rearrange into a container: case, purse, scrip and sack

explanation.walkthrough: A scrip is an old word for a small bag or wallet. Each of the four words is a container with its letters jumbled, which gives the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an assortment of different things, which is what a miscellany is.

clue.text: Murderer looking back at white crystalline substance

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis, the first murderer
at and in both mean located somewhere, as in 'at home' or 'in'

explanation.surface: A killer glancing back at a mysterious white powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Niacin, vitamin B3 or nicotinic acid, is a white crystalline compound.

clue.text: My beloved sons go to take the Knowledge

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son or sons
to go, informally, is to urinate, to wee
taken as written
art can mean learned skill or know-how

explanation.surface: A parent proudly reporting that their sons are going off to learn the Knowledge, the London cabbies' test.
explanation.walkthrough: The Knowledge is the exam London taxi drivers sit on the city's streets; here the word is just knowledge or skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone my sweetheart is an endearment for a lover, the person you hold dear.

clue.text: Change involving a single act of forfeit

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the first word encloses the next

parts.note: to waver is to shift or fluctuate
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A one-off change of rules that means somebody loses out.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving up a legal right or claim voluntarily is a relinquishment, so it is a deliberate surrender.

clue.text: Extreme happiness outsiders are unable to attend occasion

indicators.note: the outsiders, the end letters, cannot come, so they are left off

parts.note: felicity is great joy or bliss

explanation.surface: A joyous event spoiled because outsiders could not come.
explanation.walkthrough: Occasion is a verb here, to bring about, not a noun meaning event.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit a reaction is to draw it out or bring it about, the verb sense of occasion.

clue.text: Can device finish off extended answer?

indicators.note: to finish something off here means taking away its finish, its last letter

parts.note: something wide is broad or extended
to get the phone is to answer it

explanation.surface: Asking whether a gadget could complete a long answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Can reads as a verb but is the noun, a beer can.
explanation.definitionFit: A widget is the nitrogen-filled plastic device in a beer can that makes the beer foam when opened.

clue.text: Dropping off obscure suggestion for those attending

parts.note: to obscure is to dim

indicators.note: those attending a performance hear it, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: an innuendo is a sly suggestion

explanation.surface: Someone nodding off as a murky hint is dropped to an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping off sounds like falling asleep, but it is volume dropping.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a diminuendo is a gradual decrease in loudness, so the sound tails away.

clue.text: Which nasal pattern?

parts.note: one of the two nasal consonants of English
asking which means choosing one or the other
the other nasal consonant, the alternative to the first

explanation.surface: Someone asking which nasal pattern, as if choosing a nose spray.
explanation.walkthrough: N and M are the nasal consonants, made by air through the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a standard or usual model, the regular pattern something follows.

clue.text: Figures in endless runs when opening batting for both sides

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its last letter
opening means going first, so the runs abbreviation is placed at the very front

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
to be in is to be at home
batting for both sides is slang for bisexual, shortened to bi

explanation.surface: Statistics from a cricket match where an all-rounder opened the batting for both teams.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket terms are all misdirection: in means at home and batting for both sides is slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhombi are diamond-shaped geometric figures with four equal sides, the plural of rhombus.

clue.text: Side-effects of injury made pied piper signal the arrival of a magician

indicators.note: pied printing type is type spilled into a jumble, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: piper rearranged
to herald something is to announce its coming
taken as written
a mage is a wizard

explanation.surface: The Pied Piper of Hamelin announcing a wizard's entrance, with some collateral harm along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Pied Piper reads as one name, but pied is the signal for piper.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm caused beyond the intended target is incidental or collateral, the side effects of an injury.
